title: Grateful Dead Live at Lille Fairgrounds on 1972-05-13
lineage: SBD -> Rm -> Dat -> CD -> EAC -> SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy set highlighted by a smoking Truckin' and an epic 28‑minute Other One.
ai_review.review: The Miller source delivers crystal‑clear instrument separation with only a brief glitch in the middle of The Other One, making it one of the cleaner recordings of this era. Musically the show is a powerhouse – Jerry tears into Truckin', the band launches into a spacey, 28‑minute Other One, and finishes strong with He's Gone, all delivered at a consistently high intensity.

ai_rating.rationale: All reviewers rate the show 4–5 stars and praise both performance (high energy, standout Truckin' and Other One) and recording clarity; minor glitches are noted but do not detract from overall excellence.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Very clear mix with each instrument distinct; slight feedback on Truckin' and a brief glitch at ~14 min in The Other One, otherwise clean.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Four‑track set (Truckin' → Drums → The Other One → He's Gone) with a strong opening, an expansive middle jam and a solid closer; reviewers note the second set as dynamite.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Rips on Truckin', turns up reverb for an intense Other One, tone described as perfect despite slight feedback.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is present and solid; one reviewer notes missing vocal harmonies on He's Gone but otherwise no specific criticism.
band_member_comments.Bob: Provides slashing leads on Truckin' and contributes a brief wah‑wah phrase; guitar work praised throughout the jam.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's piano and Pigpen's organ are highlighted as crystal‑clear, adding eerie fills and melodic depth to the jams.
band_member_comments.Drums: Billy (Bill) delivers jazzy, powerful drumming, especially during The Other One’s extended section.
